source_passages.quotation:
- **Strike:** Exhaust crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces instead. Check hostility. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.

- **Hostile:** Removing **one** warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves marker to Hostile (except allied battle-loss rule above). **Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.** Infamy depends on whose turn it is, rather than which side attacks: no Infamy on another player's turn, and none from Strike. Hostile status requires extra boot for moves into hostile warriors, not merely buildings/tokens.
- Aid cannot move marker out of Hostile; it can still obtain a crafted item. Coalition with Hostile faction resets its marker to Indifferent.

answer.ruling: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except when the special allied battle-loss comparison applies. On Vagabond’s own turn, battle removals of Hostile pieces score one extra VP each, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; a hostile building/token therefore gives one ordinary removal VP plus one Infamy (two total), and a hostile warrior gives one Infamy unless it was the initiating warrior. No Infamy on another player’s turn or from Strike. Aid cannot undo Hostility, though it may still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that faction has no warriors in the clearing may it remove another faction piece. Strike is not battle and yields no Infamy.

source_passages.quotation: **Vagabond coalition (9.2.8):** Cannot activate normal dominance win. With **four or more players**, during own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate dominance to coalition with another player **not already in coalition**, whose VP is lowest among players other than you (choose among ties). Put your score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, you also win, including if partner wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.part: Coalition eligibility, timing, partner and effects
answer.ruling: Vagabond cannot use normal dominance win. In a four-or-more-player game, during own Daylight at 10+ VP, activate dominance to coalition with a player not already coalitioned who has the lowest VP among all players other than Vagabond (choose among ties). Put marker on partner’s faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins by any method, including dominance, Vagabond also wins. Partners are not enemies. If partner was Hostile, it becomes Indifferent; coalition alone does not grant Allied powers.

source_passages.quotation: - **Precedence:** Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together when possible; if incompatible, faction rule wins. **Cannot is absolute** unless explicitly overridden. (1.1.)

answer.ruling: Card text overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Use general and faction rules together where compatible; if incompatible, the faction rule wins. “Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden.

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions. An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March's two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. (1.1.3, 1.4, 4.3.)

answer.ruling: If simultaneous effects lack a clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses; for battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. Marquise March’s two moves are one compound action and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird or take another action.

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions. An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March's two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. (1.1.3, 1.4, 4.3.)

answer.ruling: At-start effects happen before all other effects in that phase; at-end effects happen after everything else in that phase and before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, ordinary actions are prohibited, except actions explicitly allowed at end of Evening/turn.

source_passages.section: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Hand/deck information and agreements
source_passages.quotation: - Hand size is public, contents private: reveal/show only if explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed; actions require no consent. (1.2–3.)

answer.part: Private information, piles, agreements and consent
answer.ruling: Hand size is public but card contents private; reveal/show contents only when instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; the deck may not. Non-binding agreements do not transfer cards except as rules instruct; actions require no consent.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Hand/deck information and agreements

evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Hand/deck information and agreements

source_passages.quotation: - **Cards:** Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, even for multiple same-suit payments. **If prompted to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, you must treat your birds as that suit**; the instruction determines how many cards to give or discard. **Only a bird card can pay an explicit bird-card requirement; fox, rabbit and mouse cards cannot pay it.** Draw from shared deck top; when deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into new deck. (2.1.)

answer.ruling: When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple cards for same-suit payments; when told to give/discard non-bird cards, treat birds as that suit and follow the specified number. An explicit bird-card requirement can be paid only with a bird, not fox/rabbit/mouse.

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; finite pieces
source_passages.quotation: Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects. (1.5, G.20, G.24.)

answer.ruling: Pieces are finite and proxies are not allowed. If an instruction cannot place/take/remove everything prompted, do the maximum possible and may not voluntarily do less. This does not waive costs or prerequisites and does not excuse the Eyrie from its obligation to complete Decree actions.
answer.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; finite pieces

evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; finite pieces

source_passages.quotation: - **Place/remove/replace:** Place normally from supply/leftmost track; remove normally to supply/rightmost **empty** track space, items permanently. Replace requires both removal and placement possible; the keep's placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece. Swap ignores move/place restrictions. Spending a card means discarding it, with dominance's special destination. (G.5, G.20, G.23–24, G.31, G.33.)

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; finite pieces
source_passages.quotation: Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects. (1.5, G.20, G.24.)

answer.ruling: Place pieces from supply or the leftmost track space; removed faction pieces return to supply or the rightmost empty track space. Removed items are permanently removed. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases — Place/remove/replace; Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; finite pieces

evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; finite pieces

source_passages.quotation: - **Force:** Resolve forced actions as if affected player chose them, retaining their abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its battle decisions. (1.5.5.)

answer.ruling: Resolve a forced action as if the affected player chose it, retaining that player’s abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its own battle decisions.

source_passages.quotation: - **Place/remove/replace:** Place normally from supply/leftmost track; remove normally to supply/rightmost **empty** track space, items permanently. Replace requires both removal and placement possible; the keep's placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece. Swap ignores move/place restrictions. Spending a card means discarding it, with dominance's special destination. (G.5, G.20, G.23–24, G.31, G.33.)

answer.ruling: An enemy cannot replace a piece in the Keep clearing if replacement would require placing there, because the Keep’s placement ban cannot be bypassed by Replace. A Swap ignores move/place restrictions; it is distinct from moving or placing.

source_passages.quotation: **30 VP:** First to 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn. If multiple reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player. Removing enemy buildings/tokens gives one VP each regardless of phase or whether attacker/defender. Crafting items scores printed VP except Eyrie's Disdain. Faction scoring is described above. (3.1–2.)

answer.ruling: If multiple players reach 30 VP simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins, counting the current player as eligible.

source_passages.quotation: 1. Choose factions; determine starting player and seating randomly. Take faction boards and their listed pieces. Use Fall or Winter. Fall has no special rules; on Winter, the river divides forests just as printed paths do. Rivers are otherwise not paths.

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle
source_passages.quotation: A forest is enclosed by printed paths and clearings; it is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by just one printed path. Winter's river also divides forests. (2.2–2.4, M.1–2.)

**Slip (optional):** Move to an adjacent clearing or forest, exhausting **no boots**, even into hostile warriors. Ignore all effects preventing movement **out of** a clearing. **Forest adjacency for Slip:** a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river also divides forests as paths do.

answer.ruling: Slip may move to an adjacent clearing or forest without boots. Forest adjacency connects forests to clearings touching them without crossing a printed path and forests separated by one printed path. Winter river divides forests just like paths; Fall has no special rules.
answer.evidence: Setup — Standard Setup; Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Vagabond — Slip

evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle

source_passages.quotation: **Marquise setup (6.3):** Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put keep in any corner (starting clearing). Put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the keep clearing and adjacent clearings, in any combination respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving leftmost space empty.

answer.ruling: Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put the Keep in any corner and one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the Keep clearing and its adjacent clearings, respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks right-to-left, leaving the leftmost space empty.

source_passages.quotation: **Eyrie setup (7.3):** Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader; keep others face up nearby. Tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into the columns listed on that leader. Fill roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.

answer.ruling: Supply 20 warriors. Place one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player’s starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader; keep other leaders face up nearby. Tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into that leader’s listed columns. Place the other six roosts on the roost track right-to-left.

source_passages.quotation: **Alliance setup (8.3):** Supply 10 warriors. Put the three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw **three additional cards** face down into Supporters; these are separate from your three-card hand. Start with no map pieces or officers.

answer.ruling: Supply 10 warriors; put three bases in matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from the three-card hand. Start with no map pieces and no officers.

source_passages.quotation: **Vagabond setup (9.3):** Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger; place pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Hide one each of the **R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword** beneath the four ruins: assemble and shuffle the four stacks and return each to an empty R slot so identities are hidden. Take S-marked starting items listed on character: tea, coins and bags go face up on matching tracks, other items face up in Satchel; return unused S items to box. Place each other faction's relationship marker at Indifferent.

answer.part: Vagabond setup excluding hidden ruin items
answer.ruling: Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger and place pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Take the chosen character’s S-marked starting items: tea, coins and bags go face up on matching tracks; other items face up in Satchel; return unused S items to box. Set each other faction’s relationship marker to Indifferent.

source_passages.quotation: **Recommended faction mix (5.2):** Reach should total at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, 21 for four. Base reach: Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. The Law allows adventurous groups to use any mix totaling at least 17.

answer.ruling: Recommended total Reach: at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, 21 for four. Base values are Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. Law also permits any mix totaling at least 17 for adventurous groups.

source_passages.section: Marquise de Cat (6) — Wood production and Evening
source_passages.quotation:
**Wood production:** Birdsong places one wood per sawmill in its clearing. During Daylight, each Overwork action spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there. Both methods draw from the same finite supply of eight wood tokens.

**Birdsong:** Place one wood at each sawmill (one per sawmill if multiple share a clearing), limited by eight wood supply.

**Evening:** Draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus; discard hand down to five.

answer.ruling: In Birdsong, place one wood per sawmill, including one per sawmill sharing a clearing, limited by the shared finite supply of eight wood. Daylight Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there, using the same supply. Evening draw one card plus each uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6) — Wood production and Evening

evidence: Marquise de Cat (6) — Wood production and Evening

source_passages.quotation: - **Recruit:** One warrior at **each recruiter**; only **once per turn**. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.

answer.ruling: Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter, once per turn. If supply is insufficient to fill them all, place the maximum available and choose among eligible recruiters where they go.

source_passages.section: Eyrie Dynasties (7) — Lords of the Forest, Disdain and Leader abilities
source_passages.quotation:
**Lords of the Forest:** Win ties for rule if at least one Eyrie piece there. **Disdain for Trade:** Crafted items score only **one VP instead of printed VP** (other extra crafting-point effects still apply). Builder ignores Disdain.

| Leader | Vizier columns | Ability |
|---|---|---|
| Builder | Recruit, Move | Ignore Disdain for Trade |

answer.part: Eyrie crafted item VP and Builder
answer.ruling: Eyrie crafted items score one VP instead of the card’s printed VP; other extra crafting-point effects still apply. Builder ignores Disdain for Trade and thus does not have that one-VP restriction.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7) — Lords of the Forest, Disdain and Leader abilities

evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7) — Lords of the Forest, Disdain and Leader abilities

source_passages.quotation:
| Leader | Vizier columns | Ability |
|---|---|---|
| Builder | Recruit, Move | Ignore Disdain for Trade |
| Charismatic | Recruit, Battle | Each Recruit must place two warriors instead of one |
| Commander | Move, Battle | One extra hit as attacker |
| Despot | Move, Build | When removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, score one extra VP in addition to normal removal points |

answer.ruling: Builder has Viziers in Recruit and Move and ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic has Recruit and Battle Viziers and each Recruit must place two warriors. Commander has Move and Battle Viziers and one extra hit as attacker. Despot has Move and Build Viziers and scores one extra VP when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, in addition to normal removal points.

source_passages.quotation:
| Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |

If any required action cannot be completed fully for any reason (including warrior/building supply), immediately enter **Turmoil**; do not skip that card or continue other Decree columns.

answer.part: Charismatic Recruit with only one warrior available
answer.ruling: No. Charismatic’s one Recruit card requires placing two warriors at one chosen roost in the matching clearing. If only one warrior remains in supply, the required action cannot be fully completed, so immediately enter Turmoil; do not count the one warrior as satisfying the card.

source_passages.quotation: **Guerrilla War:** When Alliance defends, Alliance uses higher die and attacker lower; warrior caps still apply.
Each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle.

answer.ruling: Guerrilla War does not bypass warrior caps. When Alliance defends, Alliance uses the higher die and attacker the lower, while each side’s rolled hits remain capped by its own warriors in battle.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) — Guerrilla War; Shared battle dice limits

source_passages.quotation: **Supporters** are a separate face-down stack, inspectable by Alliance. They can be spent only for suit; they do not count as hand cards or toward hand limit. With no bases on map, maximum **five supporters**; incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded. With any base, unlimited supporters.

answer.ruling: Supporters are face-down and Alliance may inspect them. They may be spent only for suit; they cannot be used to craft, are not hand cards and do not count toward the five-card hand limit.

source_passages.quotation:
**Birdsong:** Both Revolt and Spread Sympathy take place **during Birdsong**. Complete **all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy**; each may be performed any number of times. **For both actions, every supporter spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild.** Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt this Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt:

- **Revolt:** Choose sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on your board. Spend **two matching supporters**. **Remove all enemy pieces there and score one VP per enemy building/token removed**; then place matching base. Place warriors there equal to number of sympathetic clearings matching the base's printed suit (including revolt clearing), and one warrior in Officers box. Score normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens. Resolve the effect even if a prompted placement cannot be completed: place the maximum possible, without adding a base-placement prerequisite. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.
- **Spread Sympathy:** Choose unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy; if no sympathy anywhere, choose any clearing. Spend matching supporters shown above next sympathy token. **Martial Law:** add one matching supporter if chosen clearing has at least three warriors of **one other player**. Place token and score uncovered space. Only one sympathy per clearing. Keep's placement ban still applies.

answer.part: Spread then Revolt in same Birdsong
answer.ruling: No. All Revolts must be completed before beginning any Spread Sympathy. Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong, so sympathy newly spread that Birdsong cannot support a Revolt then.

source_passages.section: Woodland Alliance — Spread Sympathy, Martial Law
source_passages.quotation:
**Martial Law:** add one matching supporter if chosen clearing has at least three warriors of **one other player**.

Organize spends no supporters and has no sympathy-adjacency requirement or Martial Law cost; it still needs legal token placement.

answer.part: Martial Law threshold and Organize cost
answer.ruling: No. Martial Law requires at least three warriors belonging to one other player; two warriors from each of two players do not meet it. Martial Law adds a matching supporter to Spread Sympathy, but Organize has no supporter cost, adjacency requirement, or Martial Law cost.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Spread Sympathy, Martial Law

evidence: Woodland Alliance — Spread Sympathy, Martial Law

source_passages.quotation: **Outrage:** Each time another player **removes sympathy** or **moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing**, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters. Moving a group costs one card per affected move, rather than one per warrior. If no matching cards including birds, show hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. **If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; payment or the no-match draw still occurs.** Merely battling there is not a trigger unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors there and moving only Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.

- **Move:** May force warriors of **one** Allied faction to accompany the pawn to its destination clearing. They follow their own movement restrictions, including rule and Eyrie tie advantage. They cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. Moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage.

**Outrage:** Each time another player **removes sympathy** or **moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing**, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters. Moving a group costs one card per affected move, rather than one per warrior. If no matching cards including birds, show hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. **If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; payment or the no-match draw still occurs.** Merely battling there is not a trigger unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors there and moving only Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.

answer.part: Outrage for placement, pawn movement, allied warriors
answer.ruling: Placing warriors in sympathy does not trigger Outrage, and moving only Vagabond’s pawn there also does not trigger it. If Vagabond moves warriors of one Allied faction into a sympathetic clearing, that move triggers Outrage because warriors moved in; the moving group costs one matching hand card per affected move, regardless of warrior count.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) — Outrage; Vagabond — Allied benefits / Move

source_passages.quotation:
**Evening:** The four military operations are **Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize**. Take **up to your number of officers** in operations, in any order and repetition. Officers stay on the board; taking an operation does not consume an officer. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.

| Military operation | Procedure for one operation |
|---|---|
| Move | Take one move using normal movement rules |
| Battle | Initiate one battle |
| Recruit | Place one warrior at one clearing with a base |
| Organize | Remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing; place sympathy there; score the uncovered VP |

Organize spends no supporters and has no sympathy-adjacency requirement or Martial Law cost; it still needs legal token placement.

answer.part: Evening operations, officer use and draw
answer.ruling: Alliance may take up to as many operations as officers, in any order and repetition, from Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize. Operations do not consume officers. Recruit for one operation places one warrior in one clearing with a base. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.

source_passages.quotation: **Pawn and items:** Pawn is not a warrior, cannot rule or block rule, and cannot be removed. An enemy effect removing **all enemy pieces** from its clearing instead damages **three items**.
Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.

answer.ruling: The pawn is not a warrior and cannot be removed. If an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from its clearing, instead damage three Vagabond items; Revolt also uses this Vagabond exception.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Pawn and items; Woodland Alliance — Revolt Vagabond exception

source_passages.quotation: - **Battle:** Exhaust one sword to initiate. Maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals **all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down**. As defender you are defenseless only with no undamaged swords. Take hits as item damage.
One hit damages one undamaged item of your choice; ignore excess hits when none remain.

answer.ruling: Vagabond’s maximum rolled hits as attacker or defender equals all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or down. As defender it is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. Exhausted but undamaged swords count; damaged swords do not. Hits damage one chosen undamaged item apiece, and excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Battle; Vagabond — damage from hits

source_passages.quotation:
Items may be face up (ready) or face down (exhausted), and independently undamaged or damaged. To exhaust for an action, choose a face-up **undamaged** item and flip it down. Damaged items cannot pay actions.

Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting an item on track sends it to Satchel. Boots/swords/crossbows/torch/hammers are gained face up in Satchel. Damaging an item sends it to Damaged box **without changing its face**. One hit damages one undamaged item of your choice; ignore excess hits when none remain.

answer.part: Item tracks and action payment condition
answer.ruling: Face-up tea, coins and bags in Satchel immediately move to an empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of that type. Exhausting an item on a track sends it to Satchel. Damaged items go to Damaged box without face change. To exhaust for an action, item must be face-up and undamaged; damaged items cannot pay actions, even if face-up.

source_passages.quotation: 4. **Capacity, the last step of Evening after drawing and discarding:** Satchel **plus Damaged box** may contain **six items plus two per face-up bag on its track**. Track items do not count toward load. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit. Do not check capacity immediately upon acquiring an item.

answer.ruling: At the last step of Evening, after drawing and discarding, Satchel plus Damaged box may hold six items plus two per face-up bag on its track. Track items do not count. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit. Do not check capacity immediately when acquiring items.

source_passages.quotation:
Refresh: First count tea already face up on Refresh track; flip two exhausted items face up per counted tea, then three more exhausted items. Tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh this step. Refreshing changes face, not damaged status.

Rest in forest: return all damaged items to Satchel and flip them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. This does not refresh undamaged exhausted items.

answer.ruling: Forest Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, then moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if able; it does not refresh an undamaged exhausted item. Refresh instead flips exhausted items face up according to face-up Refresh-track tea plus three, without changing damage status. Repair is an action that exhausts a hammer to move one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Refresh and Rest; Vagabond — Repair

source_passages.quotation:
- **Aid:** Exhaust **one face-up, undamaged item of any type**, give a card matching your clearing to player with faction pieces there, even Hostile. May then take one item from their Crafted Items box face up into Satchel/track; no available item is required to Aid. **Only non-Hostile relationships can advance through Aid; a Hostile recipient stays Hostile.** Check relationship improvement below.

**Relationships:** Each other faction starts Indifferent. To advance a non-Hostile marker one space, Aid that faction as many times **in this same turn** as printed between current and next spaces. One Aid counts toward only one improvement. Advance and score VP printed in new space. At final space become **Allied**; each subsequent Aid to that faction scores **two VP**.

answer.part: Aid cost, target and relationship progress
answer.ruling: Aid exhausts one face-up undamaged item of any type and gives a card matching Vagabond’s clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even if Hostile. Vagabond may then take one item from that player’s Crafted Items box face up into Satchel/track, but no crafted item is required. To advance a non-Hostile relationship one space, Aid that faction the number of times printed between the current and next spaces during the same turn; each Aid counts toward only one improvement. On reaching Allied, each later Aid scores two VP.

source_passages.quotation:
**Allied benefits:** Aid gains two VP, warriors may accompany movement, and participating warriors increase the attacking rolled-hit limit as follows:

- **Aid:** Each subsequent Aid to this Allied faction scores **two VP**.
- **Move:** May force warriors of **one** Allied faction to accompany the pawn to its destination clearing. They follow their own movement restrictions, including rule and Eyrie tie advantage. They cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. Moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage.
- **Attack with an increased hit limit:** At the start of battle **as attacker**, you may treat warriors of **one** Allied faction in the battle clearing as your own. **Add those warriors to all your undamaged swords to determine your maximum rolled hits**. They can join against a different enemy; you cannot use an ally's warriors to attack that ally itself.

**Taking hits with an ally:** In a battle using Allied warriors as your own, you may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging your items. If you remove **more allied warriors than items you damage in that battle**, the ally becomes Hostile **at battle end**. This overrides ordinary hostility timing for those friendly warriors taken as hits against the other enemy. Equal numbers do not trigger the rule.

answer.ruling: Once Allied, each subsequent Aid scores two VP. Vagabond may move warriors of one Allied faction along to the pawn destination; they follow their own movement restrictions and cannot accompany a move required to be alone. At the start of battle as attacker, Vagabond may count warriors of one Allied faction in the clearing as its own and add them to all undamaged swords for maximum rolled hits. They may fight another enemy but cannot be used to attack their own faction.

source_passages.quotation:
**Allied benefits:** Aid gains two VP, warriors may accompany movement, and participating warriors increase the attacking rolled-hit limit as follows:

- **Aid:** Each subsequent Aid to this Allied faction scores **two VP**.
- **Move:** May force warriors of **one** Allied faction to accompany the pawn to its destination clearing. They follow their own movement restrictions, including rule and Eyrie tie advantage. They cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. Moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage.
- **Attack with an increased hit limit:** At the start of battle **as attacker**, you may treat warriors of **one** Allied faction in the battle clearing as your own. **Add those warriors to all your undamaged swords to determine your maximum rolled hits**. They can join against a different enemy; you cannot use an ally's warriors to attack that ally itself.

**Taking hits with an ally:** In a battle using Allied warriors as your own, you may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging your items. If you remove **more allied warriors than items you damage in that battle**, the ally becomes Hostile **at battle end**. This overrides ordinary hostility timing for those friendly warriors taken as hits against the other enemy. Equal numbers do not trigger the rule.

answer.part: Hostility after allied warriors absorb hits
answer.ruling: At battle end, in a battle using Allied warriors as Vagabond’s own, the ally becomes Hostile if Vagabond removed more of its warriors to absorb hits than the number of items Vagabond damaged in that battle. Equal numbers do not trigger Hostility. This overrides ordinary timing for those allied warrior losses.

source_passages.quotation: - **Craft:** Exhaust one hammer per crafting icon; pawn acts as crafting piece matching current clearing, and may activate repeatedly despite normal once-per-turn crafting limit. Clearing must match **all icons**; cannot craft mixed fox/rabbit/mouse requirements from one clearing. When you craft an item, you may immediately take that item face up into Satchel/track and **use it for another Daylight action immediately**, if its cost and other requirements are met. Need supply item as usual.

answer.part: Mixed suit crafting, reuse and immediate item use
answer.ruling: No: one current clearing must match all card crafting icons, so it cannot pay mixed fox/rabbit icons. The pawn may activate repeatedly, but exhaust one face-up undamaged hammer per icon. When an item is crafted, Vagabond may immediately take it face up into Satchel/track and use it for another Daylight action immediately if that action’s costs and other requirements are met; the item must be in supply to craft.

source_passages.quotation:
| Base character | Starting items | Special action |
|---|---|---|
| Thief | boot, torch, tea, sword | **Steal:** exhaust torch to take random hand card from player with faction pieces in your clearing |
| Tinker | boot, torch, bag, hammer | **Day Labor:** exhaust torch to take discard-pile card matching clearing; bird always qualifies |
| Ranger | boot, torch, crossbow, sword | **Hideout:** exhaust torch to repair three items, keeping their faces; immediately end Daylight and begin Evening |

answer.ruling: Thief starts with boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in Vagabond’s clearing. Tinker starts with boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching the clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts with boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items preserving faces, immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.

source_passages.quotation: - **Explore:** Exhaust torch in ruin's clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track; score one VP if an item taken. Remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.
Clearings have fox, rabbit or mouse suit and limited building slots. Buildings require open slots; tokens do not occupy these. Ruins block their slots and can be removed only when explicitly allowed.

answer.ruling: Taking a ruin’s last hidden item removes the ruin and frees its building slot. Ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed; ordinary building placement cannot remove one.

source_passages.quotation: **Vagabond coalition (9.2.8):** Cannot activate normal dominance win. With **four or more players**, during own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate dominance to coalition with another player **not already in coalition**, whose VP is lowest among players other than you (choose among ties). Put your score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, you also win, including if partner wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.ruling: Coalition partners are not enemies and coalition alone does not give Allied relationship benefits; therefore a coalition partner cannot be attacked as an enemy.

source_passages.quotation: **Hostile:** Removing **one** warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves marker to Hostile (except allied battle-loss rule above). **Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.** Infamy depends on whose turn it is, rather than which side attacks: no Infamy on another player's turn, and none from Strike.

answer.ruling: The first removed warrior makes that faction Hostile and is exempt from Infamy; the second warrior, now a hostile piece removed during Vagabond’s own-turn battle, earns one Infamy VP. The building removed afterward is hostile and gives one ordinary removal VP plus one Infamy, totaling two. Total for the two warriors and building is three VP: 0 + 1 + 2.

source_passages.quotation: - **Move:** Exhaust one boot, plus **one extra boot** if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves). Ignore rule. **Cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest you may move only to an adjacent clearing.** Slip has the special free-boot exception.

answer.ruling: A destination with only hostile buildings costs one boot; extra cost is triggered by hostile warriors, not hostile buildings/tokens. A destination with hostile warriors costs two boots total even if multiple Hostile factions have warriors there: one normal boot and one extra boot, not an extra per faction.

source_passages.quotation: **Dominance (3.3):** In own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate a dominance card from hand into play area; remove score marker and stop scoring VP. Cannot remove/replace activated card. At **start of own Birdsong**, win if ruling **three clearings of matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit**, or for **bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings**. Meeting condition earlier does not immediately win. Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit. Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available instead. During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.

answer.ruling: Taking an available dominance card during your own Daylight puts it into hand but does not activate it. Activation is separate and requires at least 10 VP. Neither taking nor activating uses a faction action allowance.

source_passages.quotation: Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces. **Faction-piece ownership cannot change**: each player owns the faction chosen in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items; possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.

answer.ruling: Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns the faction chosen in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction or enemy pieces, and possession does not make an item faction-owned.

source_passages.quotation:
| Separate component after a successful craft | Starts in | Goes to |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate-effect crafting card | Your hand | Shared discard pile after resolving |
| Persistent-effect crafting card | Your hand | Your play area |
| Item token produced by an item card | Map item supply | Crafting faction’s Crafted Items box; when Vagabond itself crafts, it may immediately take its crafted item face up into Satchel/track |

- Immediate effect (paper box): resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted. Take the item token into Crafted Items and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie exception. The item token stays; the crafting card is discarded. Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does.
- Persistent effect (stone box): keep card in your play area and gain its text, subject to the personal duplicate check above. Its card is outside your hand and cannot be spent/discarded/used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

answer.ruling: Resolve an immediate-effect card then discard that crafting card; its item token stays in Crafted Items. Keep a persistent-effect card in the play area. A play-area card is outside the hand and cannot be spent, discarded or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

source_passages.quotation: - **Ambush cards cannot be crafted:** the defender may play one for two immediate hits, or the attacker may play one to foil a defending ambush, matching the clearing. **Dominance cards cannot be crafted:** activate one to change victory condition, or spend it for suit.

answer.ruling: Neither Ambush nor Dominance cards can be crafted. Defender may play a clearing-matching Ambush for two immediate hits; attacker may play a matching one to foil a defending ambush. Dominance may be activated to change victory condition or spent for suit.

source_passages.quotation:
1. Choose factions; determine starting player and seating randomly. Take faction boards and their listed pieces. Use Fall or Winter. Fall has no special rules; on Winter, the river divides forests just as printed paths do. Rivers are otherwise not paths.
2. Put score markers at 0.
6. Distribute overview cards as desired; put battle dice nearby.
7. Set up factions in their letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. Setup order is distinct from turn order.

answer.part: Starting player, seating, score markers, dice, setup order
answer.ruling: Choose factions, determine starting player and seating randomly. Put score markers at zero; distribute overview cards as desired and put battle dice nearby. Faction setup order is Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond, distinct from turn order.

source_passages.quotation: **30 VP:** First to 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn. If multiple reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player.

answer.ruling: The first to 30 VP wins immediately on any player’s turn, without finishing the action, phase or turn.

source_passages.quotation: **Battle (4.3):** Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. **Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.**

answer.ruling: To initiate battle, have your warriors or pawn in a clearing with an enemy and choose an enemy there as defender. You need not rule the clearing.

source_passages.quotation: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order.
It also chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces' removal.

answer.ruling: For battle effects at the same timing, the attacker chooses their order. When pieces are removed, the side whose pieces were removed chooses the order of effects triggered by their removal.
answer.evidence: Turn Structure — simultaneous effects; Battle — hit dealing

source_passages.quotation: 5. **Count hits:** Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker deals one extra hit for **defenseless**; Vagabond is instead defenseless if it has no undamaged swords.

answer.ruling: In Count Hits, add extra hits and subtract ignored hits. The result is the count dealt (plus the specific defenseless extra hit when applicable).

source_passages.quotation:
| Separate component after a successful craft | Starts in | Goes to |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate-effect crafting card | Your hand | Shared discard pile after resolving |
| Persistent-effect crafting card | Your hand | Your play area |
| Item token produced by an item card | Map item supply | Crafting faction’s Crafted Items box; when Vagabond itself crafts, it may immediately take its crafted item face up into Satchel/track |

- Immediate effect (paper box): resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted. Take the item token into Crafted Items and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie exception. The item token stays; the crafting card is discarded. Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does.
- Persistent effect (stone box): keep card in your play area and gain its text, subject to the personal duplicate check above. Its card is outside your hand and cannot be spent/discarded/used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.
**Disdain for Trade:** Crafted items score only **one VP instead of printed VP** (other extra crafting-point effects still apply). Builder ignores Disdain.

answer.part: Crafted item source, destination and VP
answer.ruling: The item token is taken from the corresponding item in map supply and placed in the crafting faction’s Crafted Items box. The card’s printed VP is scored, except Eyrie scores one VP instead of printed VP unless Builder ignores Disdain. Vagabond may immediately take its crafted item into Satchel/track.
answer.evidence: Crafting — card and item destination; Eyrie — Disdain

source_passages.quotation:
- **Marquise, Eyrie and Alliance cost:** For **each icon**, activate **one workshop, roost or sympathy in a clearing matching that icon’s suit**, respectively. A crafting piece gets its suit from its clearing. Combine eligible pieces as needed, but **each piece may activate only once per turn**.
- A **three-color question-mark icon** accepts any suit.

answer.part: Craft pieces, clearing suit and wildcard icon
answer.ruling: Eyrie activates roosts; Alliance activates sympathy. Each icon requires a matching-suit crafting piece and each piece activates only once per turn. The piece’s suit comes from its clearing. A three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.

source_passages.quotation:
**Daylight:** Any order and number:

- **Craft** from hand with sympathy.
- **Mobilize:** Add one hand card to Supporters. With no base on map, keep at most five supporters and discard incoming overflow; with any base, the stack has no cap.
- **Train during Daylight:** Spend a **hand card** matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers box. Supporters cannot pay Train. Each officer allows one Evening military operation; taking operations does not consume officers.

answer.ruling: Mobilize adds one hand card to Supporters; without a base the stack holds up to five and overflow is discarded, and with any base it has no cap. Craft, Mobilize and Train can be taken in any order and number, so Alliance need not finish crafting first. Train spends a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay.

source_passages.quotation: **Evening, even after turmoil:** Score the VP on rightmost empty roost-track space. Draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses; discard down to five.

answer.ruling: Eyrie scores the VP on the rightmost empty roost-track space, draws one plus uncovered draw bonuses, then discards to five. The same Evening occurs after Turmoil.

source_passages.quotation: - **Battle:** Exhaust one sword to initiate. Maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals **all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down**. As defender you are defenseless only with no undamaged swords. Take hits as item damage.
To exhaust for an action, choose a face-up **undamaged** item and flip it down. Damaged items cannot pay actions.

answer.ruling: Initiating Daylight Battle requires exhausting one face-up, undamaged sword. An exhausted sword cannot pay, even though all undamaged swords, face up or down, count toward maximum rolled hits.
answer.evidence: Vagabond Daylight Battle; Vagabond items — exhaustion

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions. An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March's two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. (1.1.3, 1.4, 4.3.)

answer.ruling: A turn is Birdsong, Daylight, Evening; turns proceed clockwise, so after Evening the next player clockwise begins Birdsong.

source_passages.quotation: Damaging an item sends it to Damaged box **without changing its face**. One hit damages one undamaged item of your choice; ignore excess hits when none remain.

answer.ruling: Each hit damages one item that is not already damaged, chosen by Vagabond. It goes to Damaged box without changing its face. Already-damaged items cannot absorb hits; ignore excess once no undamaged items remain.

source_passages.quotation:
**Evening:** The four military operations are **Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize**. Take **up to your number of officers** in operations, in any order and repetition. Officers stay on the board; taking an operation does not consume an officer. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.

| Military operation | Procedure for one operation |
|---|---|
| Move | Take one move using normal movement rules |
| Battle | Initiate one battle |
| Recruit | Place one warrior at one clearing with a base |
| Organize | Remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing; place sympathy there; score the uncovered VP |

answer.ruling: Alliance may take up to its number of officers in operations. One Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base. Operations do not consume officers.

source_passages.quotation: **Daylight:** Any order/number, as ready undamaged items permit:

answer.ruling: Vagabond may take any number of Daylight actions in any order as ready undamaged items permit. No fixed action-type order; it may repeat an action type if its costs and other requirements are met.

source_passages.quotation: - **Strike:** Exhaust crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces instead. Check hostility. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
To exhaust for an action, choose a face-up **undamaged** item and flip it down. Damaged items cannot pay actions.

answer.part: Strike cost and required item state
answer.ruling: Strike exhausts one crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; if that faction has no warriors there, another faction piece may be removed instead. The crossbow must be face-up and undamaged to pay; exhausted or damaged copies cannot pay.
